first.rationale: Promotional pricing most directly addresses the active competitive loss and has inherited evidence of acquisition and revenue lift, but its sustainability, margin impact, and downstream customer quality are unclear. Onboarding simplification is the strongest competing response to a current deterioration, yet its inherited evidence stops at adoption rather than qualified revenue. Verify both records before committing, with promotional pricing currently favored only as a guarded, targeted test.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified record shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines with evidence consistent with sustainable growth. Reject promotional pricing because its qualified-revenue lift was accompanied by a 12% retention decline and failure at first renewal. The remaining uncertainty is that qualified revenue was not directly measured for onboarding, so the experiment should track retention, conversion to qualified revenue, and cohort value rather than completion alone.
